newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish Gdansk refinery to get syndicated loan.
newsitem.headline: Polish Gdansk refinery to get syndicated loan.

text.p: A consortium of Polish banks led by Pekao SA will grant the state-owned Rafineria Gdanska SA oil refinery a loan of up to $148.5 million to cover 35 percent of the firm's investment, the refinery said.

The firm's president Wlodzimierz Dyrka said on Wednesday that the investment plan, a part of a large-scale modernisation scheme, would boost the firm's processing capacity to 4.5 million tonnes of crude in 1999 from the current 2.9 million.
"In April, we will sign an agreement on credit for financing our modernisation programme with a consortium of Polish banks led by Pekao SA," Dyrka told Reuters in an interview.
"The credit will cover 35 percent of the financing of the programme, which will cost $425 million," he added.

He said 24 percent of the whole investment plan would come from a syndicated loan arranged by Merril Lynch, 20 percent from the firm's own funds, 11 percent from the BOS environment protection bank and the government's environment protection funds and 10 percent from various export credit guarantee agencies.
"The Gdansk refinery is capable of completing the first stage of the investment programme without a strategic investor," Dyrka said.
He said that a strategic investor would be needed for the second phase of the investment programme, planned for 2000-2005, which will require investment of between $800 million and $1.2 billion.
Polish state-owned oil holding Nafta Polska has invited initial bids a minority stake in Gdansk refinery, Poland's second biggest petrol producer.
Under a government programme, the investor will be allowed to extend its equity to a majority stake after fulfilling investment promises.
The investor would also gain access to a network of 1,400 filling station belonging to state-owned firm CPN SA, whose shares are to be allocated to Polska Nafta holding.
